video_title: Do The Cavs Need To Trade Evan Mobley? Big Offseason Coming In Cleveland

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Cavs' season ended with mixed feelings, neither upset nor satisfied
quotes.excerpt: they can't be like upset, but it stops short of being satisfied.
quotes.quote: I think that sort of sums up where the Cavs' season ended, which is you they can't be like upset, but it stops short of being satisfied. And that leaves them in an interesting position going forward.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Dan Gilbert's tweet implies Cavs are committed to current core
quotes.excerpt: The Cavs are nowhere near where they need to be and they're going to do everything they possibly can to take the next step.
quotes.quote: The Cavs are nowhere near where they need to be and they're going to do everything they possibly can to take the next step. So, Brian, you've been around the NBA for a long time. The Cavs have chosen to keep their head coach, by extension keep their front office, and I think you would agree that they're not going to trade Donovan Mitchell and they're going to re-sign in some form or fashion James Harden.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Mobley is the key lever for Cavs' roster change
quotes.excerpt: he is not going to be on the Cavs if they do anything to the roster because that is the one lever they have to really pull.
quotes.quote: If the Cavs are nowhere near where they need to be and they're going to grind all summer to get there, to me that very obviously says Evan Mobley will not be on the Cavs next season. Or at least that he is not going to be on the Cavs if they do anything to the roster because that is the one lever they have to really pull to actually fundamentally change the team and truly get the player that is better than Donovan Mitchell on the roster because that is inherently the problem the Cavs have.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Knicks' playoff run was more impressive and competitive than Cavs'
quotes.excerpt: The Knicks changed their head coach. They bet that a change in head coach would change the formula.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: The Knicks also upset the Celtics last year and were pretty impressive, and...

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: Well, but hold on. Hold on. The Knicks changed their head coach.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: The Knicks didn't run it back with the same group. They bet that a change in head coach would change the formula. It wasn't we're going to run back with the exact same thing and we're going to be better. Like it would have been understandable if the Knicks had done that last year, just like it's understandable that the Cavs brought back Kenny Atkinson. But the Cavs were not good enough this year. Their playoff run was, yes, they got to the conference finals, but it was not an impressive run to the conference finals. They wheezed their way there, past two flawed teams, and again, like you said, Dan...

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: The Knicks playoff run was more impressive last year, was easier to sell the idea of that.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: For sure. And in the conference finals were competitive.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: Well, that's what I mean. They were six games. But it was a long competitive series and, you know, like...

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Cavs must make win-now move, potentially trading Evan Mobley
quotes.excerpt: If you can use Evan Mobley to get a player that's better than Donovan Mitchell right now, this is your window.
quotes.quote: It's either the Cavs run it back with this group and hope that despite all the available evidence that we have, things are going to completely change, or they look in the mirror and say, okay, if we're really committing to the Donovan Mitchell timeline, which they're going to re-sign Donovan Mitchell or they're going to try to and Donovan has said he wants to stay there, and they already made to your point, the Darius Garland for James Harden trade, which is a win-now trade. If you can use Evan Mobley to get a player that's better than Donovan Mitchell right now, this is your window. James Harden is 37 or going to be 37. It's not like he's 32 or 27. Donovan Mitchell is across 30. This is the time to win is right now, not in three years.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Mobley is a winning trade package for Giannis Antetokounmpo
quotes.excerpt: Evan Mobley is a super interesting young player who would have a lot of value... I do think that that's a winning package to get Giannis.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: I think it's enough, yeah. I think it's enough. Evan Mobley is a super interesting young player who would have a lot of value and I think whether the Bucks want to keep him, build around him, or if they want to flip him again. I think he could, I would say if you're a team in Milwaukee's position, you go back and look at what the Oklahoma City Thunder did in the wake of the Paul George trade, right? They made about, I think it was either that summer, that off season or the next one, they made about 12 trades in 12 days, right? They just kept accumulating assets. And for a team like Milwaukee, that's what you need to do. And they could turn Evan Mobley into a ton of stuff from somebody else because Evan Mobley, even though he's not as good as Giannis, he probably has more upside than Giannis for a variety of reasons. So, I do think I do think that that's a winning package to get Giannis, if they decide to do it. And, you know, I would understand if they didn't, but again, I'm just going by the logic path of what Dan Gilbert said and knowing how the Cavs operate. And like Dan Gilbert has never been somebody who's satisfied with just having a nice team. For whatever you want to say about Dan Gilbert, he's always spent money, he's always invested resources, he's always wanted to try to win at the highest level.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: When the Cavs won the championship in 2016, their slogan was all in and it was Dan Gilbert who coined the slogan.
